reply: Back seat is the bumpy seat. 🚐 Did you bounce at the humps? Hold the bar when it jumps. 😄 [CHIPS]It was fun|I sat in front|My friend sang[/CHIPS]

reply: Water bottles work best when full. 💧 Fill yours before school daily. Small sips are better than gulps. 😊 [FACT]More than half your body is water[/FACT][CHIPS]It is pink|It has a strap|I filled it[/CHIPS]

reply: Did the catch sting his hands? 🏏 Tell him one trick. Pull hands back as it lands. 🙌 [QUIZ]Softer catch: hands pulled back, or hands held stiff?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Hands pulled back|Hands held stiff[/CHIPS]

reply: The hardest minute is the first one. 💛 You did that part today. 🎒 Tell amma about your morning tonight.

prompt: tuition la sir romba fast ah pesuranga follow panna mudiyala
reply: The trick is catching the exact moment you lost the thread. 📓 Put a small dot in the margin the second it stops making sense, and keep writing. At the end you have three dots instead of one blurry hour — and three questions are easy to ask. 🙋 [CHIPS]How to ask sir|Rewrite notes at home|Sit in front[/CHIPS]

prompt: class la puthu payyan join panirukan naan epdi pesa aarambikrathu
reply: Do not start with hi and hope. 🙂 Ask something he can answer in one word: which school before, or does he play cricket. 🏏 One answer turns into two questions, and sitting beside him at lunch does more than any message. [CHIPS]If he ignores me|Introduce my friends|Talk at interval[/CHIPS]

prompt: cricket la fielding la naan catch drop panren
reply: Dropped catches are usually a hands problem, not a bravery problem. 🏏 Watch the ball right into your fingers, and let your hands ride backwards as it arrives — hard hands bounce it straight out. Ten tennis-ball catches off a wall each evening beats waiting for match chances. 🎾 [CHIPS]High catch tips|Why a tennis ball|Close-in fielding[/CHIPS]

prompt: cycle la brake pudikka bayama iruku epdi practice panrathu
reply: The front brake does most of the stopping and the back one steadies you, so squeeze both, back a whisker first, never the front alone. 🚲 Practise on flat empty ground with a grown-up nearby, starting at walking speed. 👀 [STEPS]find flat empty ground|roll at walking speed|squeeze back then front|stop beside a chosen line[/STEPS][CHIPS]Stopping in rain|Why front is stronger|Check my brakes[/CHIPS]

prompt: school bus la window seat ku daily sanda
reply: Every bus has this same fight. 🚌 It stops the day there is a rule nobody can argue with — window by day, you Monday, him Tuesday. Then the paper takes the blame instead of you two. 📝 [STEPS]write the days in a column|put one name per day|stick it inside the bag[/STEPS][CHIPS]If he refuses|Swap for something|Sharing other things[/CHIPS]

prompt: paati ooru la irundhu vanthirukanga naan enna kelvi kekalam
reply: Ask the questions nobody thinks to ask. 👵 The second telling of a story usually carries more detail than the first, so let her tell it twice and write down the extra bits. ✏️ [STEPS]ask what she ate at your age|ask what one rupee bought|ask what her street sounded like|ask her to tell it again[/STEPS][CHIPS]Questions about her school|Questions about food|Write her story[/CHIPS]

prompt: market la thakkali rate nethu vera innaiku vera yean
reply: Vegetable prices move because vegetables cannot wait. 🍅 Tomatoes ripen in a rush, travel by lorry and spoil in days, so when many lorries reach the market on one morning the price falls, and after heavy rain damages the crop it climbs. 🚚 [QUIZ]Many lorries arrive at once, does the price go up or down?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Price goes down|Price goes up[/CHIPS]

prompt: padam paakum bothu climax la ellarum azhutanga naanum azhuthen
reply: Crying at a film is your brain doing its job. 🎬 It does not fully separate a story from real life, so it runs the character's trouble like a practice round and your body joins in. Watch for the music starting before the sad thing happens. 🎵 [CHIPS]Why music moves us|Films and silence|What is a climax[/CHIPS]

prompt: மழையால் school leave, வீட்ல என்ன பண்ணலாம்
reply: A holiday that arrives without warning is the best kind. ☔ Build something that needs a whole table — a fort, a card tower, a paper city. 🏰 Here is a rhyme for the day: [POEM]The bell did not ring, the gate stayed shut, the road wore a river, the sky poured a cup, and a whole spare day came falling down with nothing at all planned in it.[/POEM][CHIPS]Card tower tips|Indoor games list|Paper boat rules[/CHIPS]

prompt: kadaisi paper mudinjathum class la ellarum kai thattinom
reply: That clap is the best sound of the school year. 👏 Now do the part that feels lazy but is not — leave the books shut for a couple of days. 🎉 [FACT]Your brain files new memories while you sleep[/FACT][CHIPS]Holiday plan ideas|Why rest helps memory|Games for cousins[/CHIPS]

prompt: kovil la yaanai irukku adhu enna sapdum
reply: Only plants: grass, leaves, bark, banana stems, coconut fronds and fruit. 🐘 Leaves carry very little energy for such a huge body, so the eating almost never stops. Shade, water and long walks matter just as much, because heat is hard on an animal that size. 🌿 [FACT]An elephant spends most of its day eating[/FACT][CHIPS]Why the ears flap|What mahouts do|Wild elephant food[/CHIPS]

prompt: friend veetla night stay panna kupitirukan first time
reply: First sleepover is mostly logistics. 🎒 Your parents ring his parents, you carry your own brush and a change of clothes, and you settle one thing before you go: if you want to come home at eleven, you can, no explaining. Knowing that is usually why nobody needs it. 🌙 [CHIPS]What to pack|Games for night|If I feel homesick[/CHIPS]

prompt: library period la enna book edukurathu nu theriyala
reply: Do not read the back cover, read page one. 📖 Many teachers use a five-finger test for whether a book fits you today. 🖐️ [STEPS]open any page in the middle|read it at normal speed|raise a finger for each impossible word|five fingers up means try later[/STEPS][CHIPS]Books about cricket|Something funny please|Try a comic[/CHIPS]

prompt: school um tuition um rendumey iruku time manage panna mudiyala
reply: Timetables fail because they plan hours you do not actually own. 🕐 Start from the gaps that really exist, and put the subject you avoid most into the first one, while you are still fresh — the hardest thing deserves your best attention, not your leftovers. Then keep one evening a week completely empty and defend it, because a plan with no slack breaks the first time a bus runs late. [STEPS]list the real gaps in your week|name each gap by its time|put the avoided subject in the first gap|leave one evening with nothing planned[/STEPS][CHIPS]Beating procrastination|A weekly plan|When to revise[/CHIPS]

prompt: class leader ah select panirukanga epdi handle panrathu
reply: Start where it is easiest to be fair. 📋 Do the dull parts yourself, collecting the sheets, leaving last, because a leader who takes the worst job first gets listened to without raising their voice. And when you have to report something, tell the person before you tell the teacher; being surprised is what people actually resent. [CHIPS]If friends get angry|A noisy class|Talking to teachers[/CHIPS]

prompt: opening batting varuven aana first over la out aiduven
reply: Openers are not judged on runs in the first over, they are judged on still being there. 🏏 The new ball moves most early, so play as late as you can under your eyes, keep the bat coming down straight, and leave anything wide of off stump. Judging a leave well is a real skill, not laziness. [FACT]Openers face the newest hardest ball of the innings[/FACT][CHIPS]Playing the ball late|Judging a leave|Facing swing[/CHIPS]

prompt: paati ku smartphone use panna kathukanum epdi start panrathu
reply: Teach one whole task, not the phone. 📱 Pick the thing she actually wants, a video call with her sister, and walk that single path until she can do it alone; a tour of the settings teaches nothing. Two rules make it stick: make the text bigger first, and never take the phone out of her hands to do it faster. [STEPS]make the text bigger|do the task together once|let her do it alone|write the steps on paper[/STEPS][CHIPS]Scam call warning|Teaching video calls|Saving contacts[/CHIPS]

prompt: school ku 5 km cycle la poren gear cycle vaanganuma
reply: Gears do not add power, they trade it. 🚲 A low gear turns the wheel less for each push of the pedals, so a slope feels easier but you pedal more times; a high gear does the opposite on flat road. Over five flat kilometres a single-speed cycle is genuinely fine, and gears earn their price on hills, headwind and load. Ride your route once and count the climbs before you spend. [CHIPS]How gears work|Cycle maintenance basics|Riding in traffic[/CHIPS]

prompt: படம் பாக்கும்போது subtitles போட்டு பாக்கறது நல்லதா
reply: Yes, and the most useful kind is the one people usually switch off. 🎬 Same-language subtitles, Tamil audio with Tamil text, pin a sound you already understand to spelling you are still learning, which is exactly why they get used to build reading practice. Translated subtitles are different: your eyes take over and your ears can quietly switch off. Try one film each way and notice which one you hear. [CHIPS]Learning by listening|Why dubbing feels off|Reading speed tips[/CHIPS]

prompt: market la amma bargain panranga naan panna awkward ah iruku
reply: Watch amma next time: she names a number, half turns away, the vendor calls her back. 🛒 It is a script both sides know, not a fight, and the friendly part is not decoration — it is what keeps that shop glad to see you next week. With a farmer selling their own produce, many families simply pay what is asked. [STEPS]ask the price at two shops first|decide your number before you speak|say it once and stay friendly|be willing to walk away[/STEPS][CHIPS]What to say first|When not to bargain|Checking market rates[/CHIPS]

prompt: kovil la kumbabishekam nadakuthu adhu yean panranga
reply: It is a re-consecration ceremony. 🛕 Kumbham means pot: water and other offerings carried in pots are poured over the temple's towers, and many temples hold it after major repair work rather than every year. For the town it doubles as a deadline, since the plastering, the painting and the cleaning all get finished for that date. Families gather the way they do for a wedding. [CHIPS]What the pots hold|Why temples are painted|Who decides the date[/CHIPS]

prompt: school bag weight thanga mudiyala thol valikuthu
reply: Where the weight sits matters as much as how much it is. 🎒 Load the heaviest books flat against your back instead of in the outer flap, use both straps and tighten them so the bag rides above your hips, and take out whatever tomorrow's timetable does not need. If the ache is still there after the bag comes off, tell a grown-up rather than getting used to it. [CHIPS]Packing by timetable|Why both straps|Stretches after school[/CHIPS]

prompt: friends kooda group study panrathu nalla ideaya waste ah
reply: It works or it wastes an evening, depending on one thing: whether anyone is being tested. 📚 Reading the same chapter side by side does almost nothing, but taking turns explaining a topic with the book closed does, because pulling an answer out of memory strengthens it far more than putting it in again. [QUIZ]Which builds memory more, rereading notes or explaining with the book shut?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Explaining with book shut|Rereading notes[/CHIPS]

prompt: serial la ad romba varuthu yean ithana ad podranga
reply: Because you are not the customer, the advertiser is. 📺 A free channel sells attention, so the more people watching at nine o'clock, the more a slot in that gap is worth, which is why the break lands exactly when something is about to be revealed. Spot that pattern once and the ads stop working on you quite so well. [QUIZ]When does the break usually land: at a dull moment, or just before a reveal?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Just before a reveal|At a dull moment[/CHIPS]

prompt: thatha daily paper padipparu naan phone la news paakuren difference enna
reply: The real difference is who decides what you see. 📰 A newspaper is edited once for everybody and it ends; thatha finishes the last page and knows he is done. Your feed is assembled for you alone, never ends, and rewards whatever holds attention, which is not the same as whatever matters. Read his paper for a week and count the stories your feed never offered you.

prompt: veetla mazhai neer sethukka pit vachirukanga adhu epdi velai seyyum
reply: Roof, pipe, filter, ground. 💧 Rain landing on the terrace runs down the pipe, passes through a gravel-and-sand filter that catches leaves and grit, and goes into a pit where it soaks into the earth instead of running off to the storm drain. That water quietly refills what borewells draw from, which is why Tamil Nadu made harvesting a rule for buildings. Clean the filter before the monsoon. [CHIPS]Why the filter matters|Storing versus soaking|Checking before rain[/CHIPS]

prompt: canteen la interval queue romba nedusa iruku
reply: Queues grow at the slowest step, not the busiest-looking one. 🍟 If paying takes longer than handing over the food, adding another server changes nothing, while separating the cash counter from the serving counter does. It is why many banks use one line feeding many counters instead of a line at each. Watch tomorrow for where people stand still; that spot is the bottleneck.
